name: build-ribbon
description: build or change the RibbonScope scope Use when you need to build or change the RibbonScope scope
---

Read all necessary skills and specs, then build or change the RibbonScope scope according to what already exists in the codebase.
If nothing has been built, start from scratch.
If you're not starting from scratch, analyze the existing codebase against the spec and determine what needs to be changed and/or refactored. It might be small changes or additions, or it might be a large refactor.  No matter the scale, make sure the spec acts as the source of truth and the code is reworked to match the spec.

# Refactoring

Always build from the latest spec, checking what's already build in [RibbonScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md) against the spec.  Spec is the source of truth, and the code should be refactored to match the spec.

# Belay Shape

Use the directory structure of ../../reference/shape to guide how to structure and organize the code.  If the shape changes, refactor the code to match.
Do not use the structure of the spec to fundamentally guide the layout of the application.  The only guidance you should look at for structure/organization is ../../reference/shape.

content.content:
shape: {RibbonShape}

shape RibbonShape:
    description:
        A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab
        component with its default styling. Its tabs are, in order: Project,
        Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on
        Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups.
        There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

    openingSeveralTabs:
        Clicking a tab opens it alone, as usual. Ctrl+clicking one (Cmd+click on
        macOS) opens it alongside whichever tabs are already open, or, if it is
        already open, closes it, so any number of tabs can be open at once. The
        last open tab can't be closed this way: Ctrl+clicking it leaves it open.
        Every open tab shows as selected.

        The command area then holds the groups of every open tab side by side,
        in the order of the tabs rather than the order they were opened, with no
        divider between one tab's groups and the next, as between any groups. An
        open tab with no commands adds nothing, and "No commands yet" shows only
        when none of the open tabs has any. When the groups are wider than the
        window, the command area scrolls sideways. The command area stays the
        same height however many tabs are open.

input.command:
cat > spec/agent/skills/ChangeRibbon.pi <<'EOF'
use @piton/belay

from /ui/components/ribbon import RibbonScope
from /ui/components/ribbon/project-tab import RibbonProjectTabScope
from /ui/components/ribbon/code-tab import RibbonCodeTabScope
from /ui/components/ribbon/spec-tab import RibbonSpecTabScope
from /ui/components/ribbon/research-tab import RibbonResearchTabScope
from /ui/components/ribbon/application-tab import RibbonApplicationTabScope

export skill ChangeRibbon:
    description:
        change the main ribbon's tabs, groups, or commands, keeping the spec
        of each tab in its own scope
    useWhen:
        you're asked to add, change, move, or remove anything in the main
        ribbon, such as a command, a group, or a whole tab
    prompt:
        The ribbon's spec is split by tab. @{RibbonScope} describes the ribbon
        as a whole: the order of its tabs, opening several at once, collapsing,
        the project's name and the activity spinner, and how groups are laid
        out. What each tab holds, its groups in order and each command's label,
        icon, tooltip, what it does, when it's disabled, and whether it stays in
        the collapsed ribbon, is described in that tab's own scope, one per tab,
        in a folder of its own under the ribbon:
        - @{RibbonProjectTabScope}, in project-tab
        - @{RibbonCodeTabScope}, in code-tab
        - @{RibbonSpecTabScope}, in spec-tab
        - @{RibbonResearchTabScope}, in research-tab
        - @{RibbonApplicationTabScope}, in application-tab

        Every change to the ribbon starts with the spec, which is the source
        of truth, and then the code is made to match it.

    changingATab:
        To add, change, move, or remove a command or group within a tab, edit
        that tab's scope, never the ribbon's. Describe each group under the
        tab's groups, in order, and each command under its commands, with its
        label, icon, tooltip, what clicking it does, when and why it is
        disabled, and whether it is primary, staying in the collapsed ribbon. A
        command that opens a scope of its own references that scope rather than
        repeating what it does. A tab left with no commands says it reads
        "No commands yet".

    addingATab:
        To add a tab, create a new scope for it rather than describing it in
        the ribbon's scope: a folder under the ribbon's, named for the tab in
        kebab case followed by -tab, holding an index.pi that exports a scope
        named Ribbon, then the tab's name, then TabScope, with a concept and a
        shape following the other tabs', giving its pitch, its groups, and its
        commands. Then, in @{RibbonScope}, import the new scope, reference it,
        and add the tab where it belongs in the order of the tabs. Removing a
        tab is the reverse: delete its folder, and take it out of the ribbon's
        scope.

    changingTheRibbon:
        Only what applies to the ribbon as a whole, rather than to one tab,
        changes @{RibbonScope}, such as the order of the tabs, how open tabs
        and groups are laid out, or collapsing.

    code:
        Each tab's commands live in its own module under the ribbon's code, one
        per tab scope, and the ribbon's own module holds the tabs, the order
        they're in, and the layout. Keep the two in step: a new tab scope gets
        a new module, a tab's commands change only in its module, and a tab
        added or removed is added to or removed from the ribbon's list of tabs.

    checking:
        After changing the spec, run piton check over the spec and
        piton build check, then piton build, so the compiled reference and
        skills are up to date, before changing the code.
EOF
cat spec/agent/skills/index.pi; echo 'from ./ChangeRibbon export *' >> spec/agent/skills/index.pi; piton check $(find spec -name '*.pi') system-prompts/*.pi 2>&1 | tail -3 && piton build check 2>&1 | tail -1 && piton build 2>&1 | tail -1; ls .claude/skills/

---
name: change-ribbon
description: change the main ribbon's tabs, groups, or commands, keeping the spec of each tab in its own scope Use when you're asked to add, change, move, or remove anything in the main ribbon, such as a command, a group, or a whole tab
---

Change the ribbon spec first, which is the source of truth, then make the code match it. The ribbon's spec is split by tab: [RibbonScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md) describes the ribbon as a whole, and each tab is described in a scope of its own. Changes within a tab go in that tab's scope, and a new tab gets a new scope, never a section of the ribbon's.

# Spec Layout

[RibbonScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md) describes the ribbon as a whole: the order of its tabs, opening several at once, collapsing, the project's name and the activity spinner, and how groups are laid out. What each tab holds, its groups in order and each command's label, icon, tooltip, what it does, when it's disabled, and whether it stays in the collapsed ribbon, is described in that tab's own scope, in a folder of its own under the ribbon.

# Tab Scopes

- [RibbonProjectTabScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/project-tab/RibbonProjectTabScope.md), in project-tab
- [RibbonCodeTabScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/code-tab/RibbonCodeTabScope.md), in code-tab
- [RibbonSpecTabScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/spec-tab/RibbonSpecTabScope.md), in spec-tab
- [RibbonResearchTabScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/research-tab/RibbonResearchTabScope.md), in research-tab
- [RibbonApplicationTabScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/application-tab/RibbonApplicationTabScope.md), in application-tab

# Changing ATab

To add, change, move, or remove a command or group within a tab, edit that tab's scope, never the ribbon's. Describe each group under the tab's groups, in order, and each command under its commands, with its label, icon, tooltip, what clicking it does, when and why it is disabled, and whether it is primary, staying in the collapsed ribbon. A command that opens a scope of its own references that scope rather than repeating what it does. A tab left with no commands says it reads "No commands yet".

# Adding ATab

To add a tab, create a new scope for it rather than describing it in the ribbon's scope: a folder under the ribbon's, named for the tab in kebab case followed by -tab, holding an index.pi that exports a scope named Ribbon, then the tab's name, then TabScope, with a concept and a shape following the other tabs', giving its pitch, its groups, and its commands. Then, in [RibbonScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md), import the new scope, reference it, and add the tab where it belongs in the order of the tabs. Removing a tab is the reverse: delete its folder, and take it out of the ribbon's scope.

# Changing The Ribbon

Only what applies to the ribbon as a whole, rather than to one tab, changes [RibbonScope](../../reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md), such as the order of the tabs, how open tabs and groups are laid out, or collapsing.

# Code

Each tab's commands live in its own module under the ribbon's code, one per tab scope, and the ribbon's own module holds the tabs, the order they're in, and the layout. Keep the two in step: a new tab scope gets a new module, a tab's commands change only in its module, and a tab added or removed is added to or removed from the ribbon's list of tabs.

# Checking

After changing the spec, run piton check over the spec and piton build check, then piton build, so the compiled reference and skills are up to date, before changing the code.

Links in this document point at reference files. Read one when the work touches what it describes.

I added a `change-ribbon` skill. It's written in the spec like your other skills, at `spec/agent/skills/ChangeRibbon.pi`, and `piton build` compiles it to `.claude/skills/change-ribbon/SKILL.md`.

It's meant to be used when adding, changing, moving or removing anything in the main ribbon: a command, a group or a whole tab. It says:

- **Spec first:** change the spec first, then make the code match it.
- **Where things live:** `RibbonScope` covers only the ribbon as a whole. That means tab order, opening several tabs, collapsing, and group layout.
- **Tab scopes:** each tab has its own scope. The skill links all five: Project, Code, Spec, Research and Application.
- **Changing one tab:** edit that tab's scope, never the ribbon's. Each command gets its label, icon, tooltip, what it does, when it's disabled, and whether it stays in the collapsed ribbon. A command that opens another scope should reference that scope rather than repeat it.
- **Adding or removing a tab:** a new tab gets its own folder under the ribbon spec, named like `research-tab/index.pi` and exporting a scope named like `RibbonResearchTabScope`. It's then imported into `RibbonScope` and placed in the tab order. Removing a tab is the reverse.
- **Code:** each tab has its own module under `src/ribbon`, and `mod.rs` holds the list and order of tabs; keep these in step with the spec.
- **Checking:** run `piton check`, `piton build check`, then `piton build` before changing the code.

The tab scopes are linked by reference, so if one is renamed or moved, `piton check` fails until the skill is updated.

`piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` all ran cleanly. `.claude` is in `.gitignore`, so only the `.pi` file will be committed, and anyone else needs to run `piton build` to get the skill.
